verifiers.conditions:
Mechanism (KNOWN). A CHAIN_CORRECTED segment becomes a CHAIN_SEGMENT anchor whenever all three hold:
(i) origin !== 'DERIVED' (CC always passes);
(ii) confidence > 0 (CC is > 0 by construction unless the reading's or the token's confidence is 0);
(iii) anchorable is undefined, or it returns true.

Nothing else filters it. dependsOnScale is written but never read in source-metrics. ScaleAnchorInput and RegistrationAnchor do not carry the origin.

Because a CC value is admissible only within 2.2 px of fixedScale (chains.ts:673), and registerFrame keeps inliers within 3 px (registration.ts:87, 128), a CC anchor is an inlier of any registration scale near fixedScale. That is true by construction.

Its effect:
- it raises the kept-anchor count (+0.08 each, up to 5, registration.ts:170);
- it lowers rmsM;
- it passes the anchors.length >= 2 gate (extract.ts:793);
- one CC anchor on an axis flips measuredBothAxes and the base from 0.35 to 0.5 (:159, :170).

Its fit weight is reduced (confidence carries 0.85^subs and the reading's confidence), so it pulls the fitted scale less. The count-based confidence ignores that weight.

When it happens, by case:

A. Legacy loop, the full self-witness. Applies to:
- non-FLOOR_PLAN PLAN_XZ frames, and plans without read.raw (no metric solution);
- LEGACY_UNCONFIRMED (rereadable=false);
- CONFIRMED chains that were not re-read (offer null by sameEntries at :1303, or not better at :1313-1333).

Here solved = legacy.solved at fixedScale = the scaleX/scaleY/pooled vote. That vote itself counts substitution readings (proposalsOf over all readings). There is no minCorrectionPx, so short spans can be corrected (murajach 111→117 over 48.5 px). The CC value was chosen to fit a scale it may have seeded, and it then anchors that scale: fully circular.

B. REPLACED/ADDED. scaleStands=false, so reread is every chain but anchorable stays undefined: every READ and CC segment anchors.
- The CC values were chosen at axisScale. That is the independently selected scale, refit on INDEPENDENT decisive witnesses (metric-solution.ts:1236-1247), with minCorrectionPx = 25·tol.
- So the scale was not created by those values. The CC anchor only restates it and inflates the registration's count, confidence and rms.
- This is a weaker self-witness: it inflates confidence but does not originate the scale.

C. CONFIRMED and the chain re-read (rereadChainIds). anchorable compares the RE-READ segment, not the legacy one, against a legacy segment on equal fromPx, toPx, origin, valueCm and confidence.
- Re-read readings come from correctionReadings, where the confidence is 1 for the as-read value and the rival, and pRatio/glyph otherwise. Classic readings have confidence alt.score/glyph.score.
- So a re-read CC equals a legacy CC only by coincidence. In effect, CC anchors are blocked on re-read chains.
- MEASURED (1.8.0 sets, work005i-a/m-on plus murajach and gozdzikowcach): 0 anchors of ANY origin come from re-read chains. The filter also suppresses good re-read READ values (e.g. marcowki READ 1260).

Scope of "confirms". The registration (mpp, residual, confidence, the measuredBothAxes flag, the >=2 gate) is confirmed by the CC anchor. FrameMetricSolution (relation, confidence, witnesses) does not read anchors or segment origins, so it is NOT confirmed by them. The same loop exists for level datums: LEVEL_DATUM_PAIR anchors at extract.ts:757-771, with CC datums set at registration.ts:394 and zeroRow taken from the same ladder fit.

MEASURED: anchor origins in the sealed 1.8.0 PLAN_XZ registrations (LINEAR_DIMENSION anchors; duplicate copies not removed):

| Relation | CHAIN_CORRECTED | READ |
|---|---|---|
| CONFIRMED | 125 | 52 |
| LEGACY_UNCONFIRMED | 114 | 37 |
| NO_METRIC | 51 | 18 |
| REPLACED | 14 | 57 |
| ADDED | 1 | 4 |

Every one of these is on a chain that was not re-read.

verifiers.conditions:
How each part of S4 holds up:

(1) 'Global greedy': REFUTED. Each connected neighbourhood gets an exact minimum-cost assignment. A bound label costs cost-6 and an unassigned one costs 0. Near-ties abstain as AMBIGUOUS (margin < 0.1 text heights). It is global only within a neighbourhood. The legacy, per-orientation and final passes are three independent solves on different token sets. Only the legacy and final decisions are kept, and only for plans. The one non-optimal case: a neighbourhood whose work exceeds 6e8 is not solved, and every label in it becomes UNASSIGNED with bounded:true.

(2) 'Blind to values and scale': PARTIAL. The cost and the candidate edges are purely geometric: offset normalised by the token's own height, side convention, and optional centring. But:
- (a) A token takes part only if it has at least one LINEAR_DIMENSION reading, which makes membership value-dependent. In the legacy pass, a substitution reading is enough.
- (b) The side-convention anchors use the digit count.
- (c) The final pass's token set depends on orientation decisions, some of which are scale fits.
- (d) solveChain then re-picks which span a bound label measures, by fit to fixedScale and with no centring test.

(3) 'One label per segment': PARTIAL. Assignment enforces one label per (chain, elementary interval) slot, and solveChain enforces at most one label per solved span. Two consequences:
- An overall label printed on the same line as its part labels competes for the same interval slot.
- Two labels in adjacent intervals can never be merged into one span.

(4) 'Correct label left unbound, no explicit UNRESOLVED in MetricEvidence': CONFIRMED and wider than stated. No MetricEvidence is ever emitted for an unbound label. Its only traces are:
- (i) the plan-only dimensionTopology decision record, which reconstruction never reads;
- (ii) the aggregate gap/unattached UnresolvedMetric, which applies only to read.tokens tokens with score >= 0.25, has no chain or interval link, and gives the false reason 'not on a dimension line'.

The same loss also hits a BOUND label whose readings all miss the scale:
- segment.token stays unset (chains.ts:757);
- the span becomes DERIVED on a confirmed chain (chains.ts:780-784), described as 'nothing is printed', or otherwise a bare segment with confidence 0;
- labelled is never set, contrary to the schema;
- the token is not marked used, so it also lands in the orphan gap with the false reason.

Also possible (KNOWN from code): a token outside the tick range, or more than 2.2 heights off the line, gets no decision record at all.

A statement's `asRead` (line 228) is empty in these cases:

- (a) T1 AS_READ_REFUTATION needs `registrationRefuted >= MAJOR_SHARE` (0.5, line 882) and an alternative at least 0.25 lower (lines 1006-1018). At 0, both are impossible.
- (b) `compareReadings` (line 504) and `evidenceTuple` (line 515) rank `bucket(refutedShare)` fourth, after hard faults, gate refusals and footprint bucket. Bucket 0 is the best value.
